title: Scientists move a step toward quantum computers that can correct their own mistakes
key_facts: Researchers from Rutgers, IBM and partner institutions (including City College of New York) showed a quantum computer can monitor itself and recalibrate during a run
Used a 156-qubit IBM Heron processor with a chain of up to 100 qubits
Nearly 10,000 combined scramble and reset operations, the largest successful demonstration of the technique to date
Found a sharp tipping point from chaos to order depending on how often resets happen
Results matched theory in systems far beyond the roughly 24-qubit limit of classical simulation
No fault-tolerant quantum computer has yet been built
quote_evidence: Currently, no one has succeeded in creating such a device.
Executing nearly 10,000 combined operations and resets, the team achieved the largest successful demonstration of this technique to date.
why_it_matters_hint: A step toward the real-time error correction that fault-tolerant machines will need.
